project_handoff.name: JudgeMetrics

meta.project_type: Full-stack public judicial outcomes analytics platform
meta.starting_state: Empty folder opened in VS Code
meta.initial_scope: United States criminal courts, beginning with a single-jurisdiction proof of concept and expanding incrementally
meta.development_mode: Build a working vertical slice first, then expand data coverage

agent_role.instruction: You are the lead software architect, senior Python engineer, senior data engineer, statistical-modeling engineer, database architect, frontend engineer, DevOps engineer, QA engineer, and technical writer for this project.

Begin from the empty directory currently open in VS Code. Do not merely describe what should be built. Create the project, source files, schemas, migrations, tests, documentation, development environment, seed data, and initial working application.
Work iteratively. At every major milestone, run the relevant code, linters, type checkers, migrations, tests, and builds. Fix failures before progressing.
Keep the application runnable throughout development. Favor a functioning vertical slice over generating hundreds of disconnected placeholder files.

Do not fabricate data-source capabilities. Where government APIs, bulk files, court websites, access agreements, credentials, fees, or public-record requests are required, implement the connector interface and document what remains necessary.
Never claim that an arrest proves commission of a crime. Keep arrest, charge, conviction, dismissal, acquittal, release, sentencing, and later court events as separate concepts.

The application must report documented judicial outcomes and comparative statistics. Do not create an opaque ideological, partisan, "good judge", "bad judge", "best judge", or "worst judge" score. Users may sort objective measures, but the application must preserve the distinction between observed outcomes and normative conclusions.

mission.statement: Build a transparent data platform that connects publicly available court records, judicial assignments, case events, criminal-case dispositions, pretrial decisions, sentencing information, and subsequent observable justice-system events in order to measure and compare judicial outcomes.

The central product is not a news site or subjective judge-review site. It is a reproducible public-data analytics system where every important statistic can be traced back to source records and a documented methodology.
The long-term strategic asset is the normalized event-level justice dataset and its provenance graph. The website is an interface to that dataset.

core_questions.question: After a defendant receives a particular pretrial disposition, what observable outcomes occur within 30, 90, 180, 365, 730, and 1095 days?
How often are defendants rearrested, charged in a new case, convicted in a new case, reported as failing to appear, or found to have violated release conditions?
How do those outcomes compare with defendants of similar observable risk and case characteristics handled within the same jurisdiction and time period?

Which decisions were actually made by the judge, which were initiated by prosecutors, which resulted from statutes or mandatory rules, and which cannot confidently be attributed to a particular actor?
How much statistical uncertainty exists around every judge-level outcome estimate?
Can every published metric be reproduced from versioned source data and code?

non_goals.item: Do not infer that an arrest means guilt.
Do not infer that correlation proves a judge caused a later offense.
Do not attribute prosecutorial dismissals to judges.
Do not compare judges across incompatible case populations without risk adjustment.
Do not expose sealed, expunged, juvenile, or otherwise legally restricted records.
Do not create an overall political or ideological judge rating.
Do not merge defendants merely because their names match.
Do not scrape systems in violation of access rules, robots restrictions, contractual terms, or law.

product_principles.principle: Separate observed outcomes from causal claims.
Separate judicial actions from prosecutor, legislature, jury, clerk, and law-enforcement actions.
Show uncertainty, sample size, and missing-data limitations.
Prefer APIs and bulk public data over brittle scraping.
Minimize public exposure of personally identifying defendant information.
Treat data lineage as a first-class feature.

backend.dataframes: Polars preferred; Pandas allowed when library compatibility requires it

source.integration: Authentication API and PACER Case Locator API where appropriate.
source.warning: PACER access may involve fees and operational restrictions. Implement budget controls and never make uncontrolled paid requests.

source.name: CourtListener / RECAP
source.use: Federal dockets, RECAP material, parties, attorneys, judges, filings, case law, and PACER-derived information.

source.name: Florida Uniform Case Reporting
source.use: Understand Florida's canonical court-event structure and fields for judicial officers, case events, and related reporting.
source.warning: Do not assume the OSCA service is anonymously publicly readable. Current documentation requires coordinated credentials for web-service interaction. Treat direct access as a data-access workstream.

source.name: Florida county clerks and state trial-court sources
source.use: Criminal case data, parties, charges, dockets, judicial assignments, dispositions, and sentences where legally and technically available.
source.integration_priority: Prefer bulk exports, APIs, machine-readable downloads, or public-record requests before web scraping.

source.name: Bureau of Justice Statistics

data_source_strategy.source_policy: Before implementing a production connector, record: source owner, source documentation, access method, terms, update frequency, cost, rate limits, fields available, fields prohibited, retention restrictions, and provenance requirements.

entity.name: person
entity.description: Internal resolved person entity. Public UI should use pseudonymous IDs by default.

entity.name: person_identifier
entity.description: Store normalized source identifiers securely. Do not expose this table publicly.

entity.name: justice_event
entity.description: Generalized subsequent event used for longitudinal person timelines.

event_attribution_model.requirement: Every derived judicial metric must use only events whose attribution satisfies the metric's documented inclusion rules.
event_attribution_model.example: A prosecutor's voluntary dismissal must not be counted as a judicial dismissal merely because the dismissal occurred in a case assigned to that judge.
Mandatory release required by statute must not automatically be characterized as an independently discretionary decision by the assigned judge.

entity_resolution.objective: Connect records belonging to the same real-world judge, court, case, or person while aggressively limiting false-positive merges.

person_resolution.rule: Never merge people on name alone.
person_resolution.signal: Source-specific stable identifier where lawfully available
Date of birth or partial DOB when lawfully available
Other high-quality non-sensitive identifiers available in public records

matching_strategy.stage: Deterministic exact matching on trustworthy identifiers.
Rule-based matching for highly reliable combinations.
Probabilistic record linkage for ambiguous candidates.
Manual-review queue for uncertain high-impact matches.

thresholds.auto_match: Use a deliberately high probability threshold.
thresholds.auto_reject: Use a deliberately low probability threshold.
thresholds.manual_review: Everything materially ambiguous falls between the two.

entity_resolution.auditability: Store match features, model version, score, disposition, timestamp, and reviewer when applicable.

outcome_definitions.outcome: A new criminal court case involving the resolved person after the index event.
A qualifying new criminal charge after the index event.
A separately sourced arrest event after the index event. Label explicitly as rearrest, never as proof of a new offense.
A subsequent conviction after the index event.
A documented failure-to-appear event where the source and definition permit reliable identification.
A documented violation of release conditions.
A documented probation, parole, or release revocation.

analytics_methodology.rule: Always publish raw descriptive rates before sophisticated adjusted statistics.

descriptive_metrics.metric: Number and percentage detained where classification is reliable
New-case rate within each observation window
Rearrest rate within each observation window where arrest data exists
Judicial-dismissal rate where actor attribution is reliable

risk_adjustment.objective: Compare observed outcomes with expected outcomes for defendants having similar observable case characteristics.
risk_adjustment.baseline_model: Begin with an interpretable regularized logistic regression or hierarchical logistic model before introducing complex machine-learning models.

candidate_features.feature: Prior qualifying convictions where data is complete enough
Prior failures to appear where reliably observed
Age band when lawfully and reliably available

risk_adjustment.excluded_or_sensitive_features: Do not automatically use protected characteristics or proxies merely because they are available. Any sensitive-variable use must have a documented methodological purpose, legal review, fairness analysis, and publication rationale.
risk_adjustment.expected_probability: For eligible observation i, compute an expected outcome probability p_i using the versioned model.
risk_adjustment.expected_count: Expected_j = SUM(p_i) for all eligible observations attributed to subject j
risk_adjustment.interpretation: An O/E ratio above 1 means observed outcomes exceeded the model's expected count for the defined cohort. A ratio below 1 means observed outcomes were below the model's expected count. It must not be described as proof that the judge caused the difference.
risk_adjustment.uncertainty: Calculate confidence or credible intervals using an appropriate documented method. Consider hierarchical partial pooling because judges with small samples otherwise produce unstable extreme values.
risk_adjustment.minimum_sample_size: Suppress or flag judge-level comparative measures when the eligible sample is too small. Configure thresholds per metric and document them publicly.
risk_adjustment.temporal_controls: Compare contemporaneous cohorts where possible. Criminal law, crime levels, prosecutorial practices, bail regimes, and court procedures change over time.
risk_adjustment.jurisdiction_controls: Default comparisons should be within comparable courts and jurisdictions rather than indiscriminately comparing judges operating under different legal regimes.

model_validation.test: ROC AUC as a secondary diagnostic, not the only metric
Subgroup calibration analysis where legally appropriate

metric_presentation.judge_profile_example:
Judge Jane Example Circuit Criminal Division Coverage: Jan 2022 - Dec 2025
CASES Eligible criminal cases: 4,821 Eligible defendants: 3,940
PRETRIAL Recorded pretrial releases: 2,140 Recorded detentions: 821 Other/unknown: 979
OUTCOMES AFTER QUALIFYING RELEASE New criminal case within 90 days: 6.4% New criminal case within 365 days: 14.2% Documented rearrest within 365 days: 9.7% Failure to appear: 11.7%
RISK-ADJUSTED 365-DAY NEW-CASE MEASURE Observed qualifying events: 304 Model-expected events: 276 Observed / expected: 1.10 95% interval: 0.99-1.21
COMPARISON COHORT Same court Same general case period Comparable offense/risk mix Minimum sample threshold satisfied
IMPORTANT These statistics describe associations in available records. They do not prove that a judicial decision caused a later event.

presentation_rules.rule: Always show uncertainty for adjusted estimates.
Link methodology from every adjusted statistic.
Allow users to inspect underlying eligible cases where legally appropriate.
Do not present one composite judge score as objective truth.

features.feature: Global search: judge, court, jurisdiction, or case number
Select one objective metric at a time

frontend_design.visual_direction: Professional institutional analytics interface resembling a modern financial-data terminal or government-data research platform rather than a sensational news website.

api_rules.rule: Return methodology metadata with derived statistics.
Return sample size and coverage metadata with metrics.
Do not return private internal identifiers unnecessarily.

ingestion_framework.idempotency: Every ingestion pipeline must be rerunnable without creating duplicate canonical records.
ingestion_framework.incremental_updates: Design source connectors to support checkpoints, cursoring, modified timestamps, or source-specific incremental strategies.

checks.check: Case numbers unique within appropriate court namespace
Subsequent outcome occurs after index event
Unknown categories measured rather than silently discarded

coverage_metrics.metric: Percent of cases with identified judge

privacy_and_legal_design.rule: Use only lawfully obtained data and respect sealing, expungement, juvenile-record, privacy, copyright, contractual, and jurisdiction-specific restrictions.
Public availability at the source does not automatically mean unrestricted bulk republication is appropriate. Track source-specific publication restrictions.
Public-facing defendant timelines should remain pseudonymous during the MVP unless counsel and source rules support broader publication.
Provide a correction process and rapid suppression mechanism for demonstrably incorrect, sealed, expunged, misidentified, or legally restricted information.
Maintain an immutable internal audit trail when records are corrected while ensuring restricted data is no longer publicly exposed.
Every judge-level page must clearly explain that associations do not establish individual causation.
Before public nationwide launch, obtain legal review covering defamation, privacy, public-record republication, court-record restrictions, terms of service, data licensing, and state-specific laws.

security.requirement: Use parameterized database access through ORM/query builders.
Encrypt sensitive administrative/contact information at rest.
Dependency and container vulnerability scanning in CI.

property_tests.test: A subsequent event can never precede its index event.
Metric numerator can never exceed its eligible denominator unless explicitly defined otherwise.
Rerunning an ingestion job produces no duplicates.

integration_tests.test: API query against populated fixture database
Metric computation against known expected fixture output

testing_strategy.golden_dataset: Create a small synthetic justice dataset with known relationships and exact expected results. Use this as a permanent regression fixture for entity resolution and analytics.

requirements.item: Dismissals attributed separately to judges and prosecutors

synthetic_demo_dataset.purpose: The complete website and analytics engine must be demonstrable before production jurisdiction data is available.

initial_mvp.definition: A complete vertical slice that works locally using synthetic data plus at least one genuine public judge-data connector.

must_have.item: README containing one-command local startup instructions

florida_pilot.objective: After the architecture works against synthetic data, ingest real state criminal-court records from one Florida jurisdiction with the best lawful machine-readable data access.

selection_process.step: Evaluate Florida jurisdictions for data accessibility.
Confirm defendant matching fields that may lawfully be processed.
Select the jurisdiction with the strongest data rather than selecting solely by population.

florida_pilot.possible_candidates: Broward County and Miami-Dade County may be evaluated, but do not assume either is the best pilot until current source access is verified.
florida_pilot.first_real_metric: Prefer a metric based on new criminal court cases after a clearly identified qualifying pretrial event because court-case linkage may be more obtainable than complete independent arrest records during the earliest pilot.

phase.strategy: Add one jurisdiction at a time. Every new source gets a dedicated connector, mapping tests, coverage report, provenance record, and methodology compatibility review.

database.item: Indexes on court_id, judge_id, person_id, case_number_normalized, event_at, and source external IDs.
Composite indexes based on common metric filters.
Materialized aggregate tables for expensive public dashboard queries.
Partition very large event tables by time or jurisdiction only when actual scale requires it.

analytics.item: Use Polars/DuckDB for large batch transformations.
Do not calculate expensive longitudinal metrics synchronously in web requests.
Incrementally recompute only impacted subjects after new data ingestion.

provenance_requirement.statement: A user or analyst must eventually be able to trace:
provenance_requirement.chain: Published metric ↓ metric_observation ↓ eligible canonical events ↓ canonical cases / decisions / outcomes ↓ source_record ↓ raw source artifact ↓ source system + retrieval timestamp + checksum + parser version
provenance_requirement.requirement: If this chain cannot be reconstructed, the metric is not production-ready.

documentation_requirements.document: Project purpose, local setup, commands, architecture summary, and development workflow.
Instructions that future coding agents must follow, including architecture boundaries, testing requirements, provenance rules, and commands that must be run before completing work.
Definitions, equations, cohort construction, models, and limitations.
Publication, suppression, correction, and PII policy.
Current phase, completed items, unresolved issues, and next milestones.

local_development_commands.desired_interface: make install make up make migrate make seed make dev make test make lint make typecheck make ingest-fjc make compute-metrics
local_development_commands.requirement: If Make is not the optimal cross-platform abstraction, provide equivalent documented scripts while preserving simple top-level commands.

definition_of_done_for_any_feature.item: Frontend production build passes when frontend affected.
Data lineage preserved when data affected.

long_term_scaling_model.stage: One real judge directory plus synthetic court outcomes.
One state-court jurisdiction with complete end-to-end longitudinal analysis.
Multiple counties/circuits normalized into a common Florida schema.
Connector framework extended to states having usable machine-readable court data.
State-specific adapters feed a shared canonical justice-event model.
long_term_scaling_model.strategic_moat: The durable asset is the continuously updated cross-jurisdictional canonical dataset, entity-resolution graph, historical provenance, source adapters, data-quality history, and reproducible outcome methodology.

future_features.feature: Downloadable research datasets subject to source restrictions
Prosecutorial-outcome module kept analytically distinct from judicial metrics
Appellate reversal analytics with careful attribution

important_statistical_warnings.warning: A judge who handles a disproportionately high-risk docket may exhibit higher raw subsequent-event rates even if decision-making has no causal effect. Raw rates must therefore be accompanied by case-mix context.
Selection effects can occur when defendants are not randomly assigned to judges.
Changes in prosecutors, policing, statutes, bail law, crime conditions, court procedures, and reporting systems can create apparent changes in outcomes.
Rearrest measures are partly functions of law-enforcement activity and do not equal proven offending.
Missing subsequent events outside the covered jurisdiction can bias longitudinal measures downward.
Entity-resolution mistakes can severely distort repeat-event calculations.
Small samples create extreme but unstable observed rates.
Never conceal these limitations merely because a simplified number is easier to market.

first_session_execution_plan.instruction: Begin implementation immediately after reading this specification.
first_session_execution_plan.step: Inspect the currently open directory and confirm it is safe to initialize.
Initialize Git and create the base repository structure.
Create README.md and AGENTS.md before substantial implementation so future agents inherit the architectural constraints.
Bootstrap the FastAPI backend using uv.
Bootstrap the Next.js TypeScript frontend using pnpm.
Create the initial canonical SQLAlchemy models and Alembic migration.
Add /health and /ready endpoints and verify database connectivity.
Seed enough synthetic records to demonstrate judge search, case timelines, and outcome calculations.
Implement the first raw descriptive metrics.
Implement API endpoints for search, judges, cases, courts, and metrics.
Implement the initial frontend pages and connect them to the API.
Add tests and run the complete local test/build suite.
Implement the Federal Judicial Center import as the first real external-data pipeline.
Update README with exact working commands and screenshots or descriptions of the current application state.

project_handoff.first_milestone_expected_result:
When the first milestone is complete, I should be able to:
1. Clone/open the project. 2. Run one documented setup command. 3. Start PostgreSQL. 4. Run migrations. 5. Seed the synthetic dataset. 6. Start the FastAPI backend. 7. Start the Next.js frontend. 8. Open the website. 9. Search for a synthetic judge. 10. Open the judge's profile. 11. View case volume and objective outcome metrics. 12. Open an underlying synthetic case. 13. View its event timeline and provenance. 14. Return to the judge page. 15. Compare the same metric against the judge's defined comparison cohort. 16. Open the methodology page and see exactly how that metric was calculated. 17. Run the complete automated test suite successfully.
No production court data is required to satisfy this first milestone.

agent_working_rules.rule: Do not spend the entire session writing architecture documents. Build working software.
Do not prematurely implement national-scale infrastructure before the vertical slice works.
Do not create fake production integrations merely to make the application appear complete.
When external access is unavailable, create a proper adapter interface plus fixtures and document exactly what credential/access step remains.
Prefer explicit readable code over excessive abstraction during the MVP.
Use deterministic random seeds for synthetic test data.
Keep source-specific parsing separate from canonical-domain logic.
Keep statistical methodology separate from presentation logic.
Any transformation from source record to published metric must be reproducible.
Keep a TODO/roadmap containing unresolved data-access questions instead of silently inventing answers.
Update AGENTS.md whenever an architectural decision is important for future AI coding sessions.

source_verification_instructions.instruction: Before implementing live integrations, verify the latest official documentation rather than relying permanently on this specification.

project_handoff.ultimate_product_concept:
The finished platform should behave like a data terminal for the American court system:
SEARCH ↓ JUDGE / COURT / JURISDICTION ↓ OBJECTIVE CASE AND OUTCOME METRICS ↓ RISK-ADJUSTED COMPARISON ↓ CONFIDENCE / SAMPLE SIZE / COVERAGE ↓ UNDERLYING CASES ↓ EVENT TIMELINES ↓ ORIGINAL SOURCE PROVENANCE ↓ PUBLIC METHODOLOGY
The platform's credibility must come from traceability rather than rhetoric.
A user should be able to move from:
"Why does this statistic look unusual?"
to:
"What cases generated it?"
to:
"What decision occurred?"
to:
"Who was the responsible actor?"
to:
"What later observable event was counted?"
to:
"What government/public source supports it?"
to:
"How was this number calculated?"
without leaving the analytical framework.

start_now.instruction: Build the first runnable vertical slice rather than returning another design proposal.
Make reasonable engineering decisions autonomously when this specification leaves a minor implementation detail open.
Do not ask for confirmation for ordinary technical choices that can easily be changed later.
Stop and request user intervention only when credentials, paid access, legally restricted data, destructive operations, or an externally consequential choice genuinely requires it.

At the end of each implementation session, report: files created or changed, architecture implemented, commands executed, test results, what currently works, known issues, external access still needed, and the next concrete development milestone.
